subject: physics_2
question_text: What is the magnetic moment associated with a solenoid?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are both STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: M = NiA for a solenoid of N total turns, current i and turn area A; for circular turns of radius a, A = πa², so M = n·i·πa² with n the total number of turns. The book (p36) prints this formula garbled as 'M = n2l × i × ða²' — π mis-set as 'ð' and a bar magnet's length 2l mixed in; the card writes the correct form and records the book's version in the formula step's why.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Bar-magnet behaviour
lines: A current-carrying solenoid behaves like a
bar magnet. Its magnetic moment points
along the axis of the solenoid, given by
steps.margin_note: First mark. Say what the moment of a solenoid is — a bar-magnet-like moment along its axis.
steps.why: Each turn of the solenoid is a current loop with moment iA along the axis, and the turns all point the same way, so the whole solenoid acts as one magnet with the moments added.
common_mistakes: Saying the moment points across the turns. It points along the axis, the way the field of a bar magnet does.

recall.must_convey: That a current-carrying solenoid acts like a bar magnet with its magnetic moment along the axis.
accept: solenoid behaves like a bar magnet

steps.memory_tip: Every turn is a small magnet pointing the same way along the axis — the solenoid is their sum.

steps.label: The formula
lines: For a solenoid with total number of turns
n (also written N), current i and turn
radius a, the area of one turn is A = πa².
steps.margin_note: Second mark. One turn contributes iA; n turns contribute n times that.
steps.why: One current loop has moment iA, so n identical turns give M = niA = n·i·πa². The book (p36) prints this as M = n2l × i × ða² — π is mis-set as ð, and a bar magnet's length 2l has been mixed in. A solenoid's moment has no 2l in it; write M = NiA = n·i·πa².
common_mistakes: Copying the book's printed M = n2l × i × ða². The 2l belongs to a bar magnet (M = m × 2l) and ð is a misprint of π.
Using n as turns per unit length here. In this formula n is the total number of turns.

recall.must_convey: That the moment is M = NiA — total turns times current times the area πa² of one turn.

steps.memory_tip: One loop gives iA; a solenoid just multiplies by the number of turns — NiA.

insider_note: The book's printed formula for this very question is garbled — students who memorise the page reproduce a bar-magnet 2l that does not belong; M = NiA is the whole answer.
